title: Nonhalting probability under repeated runs
statement: Let $q$ be a procedure that returns either an output or no output on a finite bit string, and let $t,m$ be natural numbers with $0<t$. For any natural number $s<t$, consider the procedure that repeatedly runs $q$ on successive blocks of $t$ bits, stopping at the first output and returning no output if no such output occurs. On a uniformly random string of $mt+s$ bits, its probability of returning no output equals the $m$th power of the probability that $q$ returns no output on a uniformly random string of $t$ bits.
